p1s.summary: One arithmetic claim in Section 2 — 'The search on the full histology name was re-run cleanly after the fix, the same afternoon. It returned 23 studies against a reported total of 23' — is not traceable to any of the three cited source artifacts, nor to any file named in Section 7's Data Availability. It is not contradicted by anything, but it is currently an unverifiable number sitting in a document whose whole rhetorical strategy is 'read the artifact, don't trust the restatement.'
p1s.evidence: Searched fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json exhaustively (grep for every literal '23' substring, and for 'ct_emc_full_fixed'/'ct_emc_all'/'ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma') — no field records a post-fix re-run of the EMC-histology condition search, nor any totalCount of 23. adj.json and nonus.json are the wrong endpoints structurally (adjudication and non-US sweep respectively) and also contain no such figure. Section 7's Data Availability lists only the three named files plus four URL manifests and one status file, none of which are cited for this specific re-run. This is the one number in the document I could not independently confirm against a committed artifact.
p1s.fix: Either cite the specific literature-cache commit/payload that recorded the clean 23/23 re-run (Section 7 already names commits and payload IDs for other claims — the same discipline applied here would close the gap), or soften to 'a subsequent, uncommitted re-run returned 23 of 23' if no artifact backs the exact count.

p1s.summary: The verbatim NCT05918640 eligibility quote is presented as a complete sentence but is actually a truncated clause of a longer sentence, with a manuscript-inserted period at the truncation point.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript table (line 144): 'verbatim: *Patients must have a known FET fusion (fusion that contains EWSR1, FUS, or TAF15)*.' The source artifact's verbatim_eligibility_sentence (fet.json, task_1 record for NCT05918640) is: 'Patients must have a known FET fusion (fusion that contains EWSR1, FUS, or TAF15) as documented by next generation sequencing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH).' The quoted fragment is accurate word-for-word up to its cutoff and does not change the criterion's meaning, but labeling a mid-sentence fragment 'verbatim' with a manuscript-added closing period is a minor precision gap that a future edit for length could worsen (e.g. if a later trim moved the cut point across a comparison operator or qualifier).
p1s.fix: Either quote the full sentence, or mark the truncation with an ellipsis (e.g. '...TAF15) [as documented by NGS/PCR/FISH]') so 'verbatim' cannot be read as 'the complete sentence'. Not required before publication — meaning is unaffected — but tightens a label that currently overstates completeness.

p1s.summary: Section 2's account of the post-fix, same-afternoon re-run of the full-histology-name search ('It returned 23 studies against a reported total of 23: those three, and NCT06239272...') is stated with the same declarative confidence as every other retrieval claim in the same paragraph, but unlike every other claim in that paragraph it carries no actions_run_id, slug, or literature_cache_commit, and the '23 studies'/'reported total of 23' figures do not appear anywhere in either research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json or research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json (the two artifacts this section otherwise draws on and that Section 7 names as holding 'every trial identifier ... and every adjudication'). I also checked the literature-cache branch history (commits 0e3b077a7, d69522f46, 76d293ade, 890612eea, 11b3177ce, 02458e005 and the full Aug-7 commit list) for a matching clean re-run payload of the EMC/myxoid-chondrosarcoma condition search and found none. The underlying NCT identifiers this claim rests on (NCT00720174, NCT05355753, NCT01189253, NCT06239272) ARE independently traceable elsewhere in fet.json/other cited files, so the paper's substantive conclusions (that the three lost records are closed studies, and NCT06239272 is the only re-surfaced admitting record) are not contradicted by anything I found -- but the specific reconciliation arithmetic ('23 against 23') is currently an uncited assertion inside a section that is otherwise scrupulous about citing the run that produced every other number.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript §2: 'The search on the full histology name was re-run cleanly after the fix, the same afternoon. It returned 23 studies against a reported total of 23: those three, and NCT06239272, the one record that lists the histology, and not one of the trials §3 reports as admitting.' Compare fet.json's own accounting, which stops at: 'Twelve records were lost that way, five of them recoverable from another payload in the same file' -- fet.json's task_1/task_2 sections and its closing 'limits_of_this_screen' block (last lines of the file) never mention a 23-study re-run, a reported total of 23, or any post-fix condition-search payload; the only condition-search payloads named in fet.json are the damaged ct_emc_all and ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma runs from the original 2026-08-07 07:55 AM ET sweep.
p1s.fix: Either add the actions_run_id/slug/literature_cache_commit for the clean re-run (matching the citation style used for every other retrieval in §2), or if that payload was not separately committed, say so explicitly (e.g. 'not separately archived; recorded here from the run log') rather than stating the 23/23 figure with the same bare confidence as the archived retrievals around it.

p1s.summary: Section 6's claim that NCT07188532 is one of the two trials §4 adjudicates as refusing this disease is not independently checkable from §4's own text — §4's two bullets describe the refusing trials only by paraphrase ('titled for fusion-positive sarcoma and then restricts eligibility to three named histologies' / 'contains the literal adjective extra-skeletal while meaning extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma'), with no NCT identifier attached to either, so the reader must infer which bullet NCT07188532 corresponds to.
p1s.evidence: §6: 'NCT07188532 shows the cost, listing *round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusion* while §4 adjudicates it as refusing this disease.' vs §4's bullets, neither of which names an NCT id: 'one is titled for fusion-positive sarcoma and then restricts eligibility to three named histologies... the other contains the literal adjective *extra-skeletal* while meaning extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma.'
p1s.fix: Attach the NCT id to the matching bullet in §4 (or state explicitly in §6 which of the two §4 bullets NCT07188532 is), so the cross-reference is verifiable without inference. Not a contradiction as written, just fragile traceability for an external reviewer checking the claim against the data files in §7.

p1s.summary: The frontmatter 'purpose' field and the Abstract/§4 use two slightly different formulations of the same 'cost of a false positive' finding, which is fine substantively (neither overclaims, and neither reintroduces the retired 'worse than no map at all' framing) but the wording drift is worth tightening for one-fact-one-place discipline.
p1s.evidence: purpose: '...so a wrong hit does real harm in a disease where every trial carries weight.' vs Abstract: '...a map that sends a patient toward a trial that will refuse them does real harm, in a disease where the number of options is small enough that each one carries weight...' vs §4: 'it is a patient or a clinician pursuing a trial that will refuse them, in a disease where the number of options is small enough that each one carries weight.'
p1s.fix: Make the frontmatter purpose field quote or closely mirror the Abstract/§4 phrasing verbatim rather than paraphrasing it a third way, per §1's one-fact-one-place rule.

p1s.summary: The Abstract's opening motivating sentence ('Patients and clinicians searching for trials search the way a diagnosis is written: by histology.') is stated as a flat, unhedged behavioral fact, but nothing in the paper's two-date registry-snapshot design measures how patients or clinicians actually search. It functions as background framing rather than a finding, and no prior round appears to have hedged it the way the rest of the document hedges everything else (e.g. 'often', 'floor', 'not established here'). It is very unlikely to be read as a data claim given the surrounding rigor, but a future reviewer applying the same skepticism the rest of the paper invites could flag it as an assumption presented as fact.
p1s.evidence: Abstract, opening sentence: 'Patients and clinicians searching for trials search the way a diagnosis is written: by histology.' No citation, no hedge, and no source artifact (fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json or emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json) measures search behavior -- both are registry-API reads, not user-behavior studies.
p1s.fix: Optional: soften to something like 'Patients and clinicians searching for trials typically search the way a diagnosis is written: by histology' or reframe as the registry-mechanics fact that actually is verifiable (the condition field, not the criteria text, is what a condition search matches) rather than a claim about user behavior. Low priority given how narrow the gap is and how well-hedged everything else in the document already is.
